title: A definition search whose pattern is a prefix (`def resolve`) is not denied while grep would also print `def resolve_file`
actual: grep -n "def resolve" m.py prints def resolve_file (line 1) and def resolve (line 5); the hook denies the search and answers only with `resolve` (line 5). Same for the recorded search `def extract` / `def resolve` in audit/searches.jsonl (#14, #591).
expected: Either the answer lists every definition the pattern matches, or the search runs (a pattern that is a prefix of other names is not one name).
why_it_matters: A deny replaces grep's output; the agent never sees the other matching definitions and, told the answer is the search's result, will not look further.

title: A definition search for one line is not denied with the whole body when grep prints one line
actual: grep -n "def finalize" f.py prints 21 chars; the hook denies with a 1023-char answer holding the full 40-line body (recorded search #290: grep 60 chars, answer 1870 chars).
expected: An answer never larger than grep's own output (#217); the body only when the search asked for context lines (-A/-B/-C) or a body.
why_it_matters: Costs tokens the agent did not ask for on every plain definition lookup, and contradicts the #217 size rule.

title: A replaced name search keeps the comment lines that mention the name
actual: With a second file in the repository, grep -rn alpha --include="*.py" . prints a comment line (a.py:6 `# alpha is called here`); the denial answer lists a.py:1, 7, 10 and c.py:2 but omits line 6.
expected: A replacement lists every line grep would print, or the search runs.
why_it_matters: The deny states the answer is the search's result (Complete); a line grep would have printed is hidden from the agent.

title: A `^def NAME` search is answered with that name's definitions in the language the pattern names, not in other languages
actual: grep -rn "^def alpha" . prints only a.py:1; the hook denies and lists a.py:1 and x.js:1 (`function alpha`), 295 chars against grep's 23.
expected: The answer is limited to what the pattern matches; a line grep would not print is not added and the answer is not larger than grep's output.
why_it_matters: An answer to a different question (definitions of alpha in any language) replaces the search, and is larger than grep's output.
